propositions: The plan-review gate's LLM judge must be stable across repeated runs (self-consistency) to support new Pass-2 sub-answers like asserted_capability_confirmed routed through the G6/E4/T3 cohort.
Per-finding Pass-3 decisions must be reproducible: re-judging the same finding three times should yield κ≥0.6 and raw agreement≥0.8 to pass the R5 gate.

Plan verdict must be stable under section-order permutation; the gate must not flip from PASS to BLOCK across different top-level section orderings (order-shuffle stability κ≥0.6, raw agreement≥0.8) before R3 adds new criteria.

Infra-level INDETERMINATE verdicts (marked by coverage.llm_unavailable or coverage.verify_failed) must be excluded as execution failures, not stable judge outcomes, and re-run until substantive decisions are collected.

E6 measures the existing gate's stochastic stability via frozen, reproducible inputs (Exp A: 50 findings from G6/E4/T3 cohort × 3 self-consistency votes; Exp B: 14 plans with ≥3 sections × 3 order permutations) without modifying src/rebar code.

A self-consistency pass (κ≥0.6, raw agreement≥0.8) unblocks R5; an order-shuffle pass unblocks R3; sub-floor results on either experiment are recorded as explicit blockers for their downstream stories.
